commit_message:
[Merged] Bug 1855142 - Ensure IndexedDabaseManager::mLocale separately; r=dom-storage-reviewers,jari

mLocale is currently initialized in IndexedDatabaseManager::Init which is
called from IndexedDatabaseManager::GetOrCreate if the manager doesn't exist.
This can be a problem when IndexedDatabaseManager::GetOrCreate is called very
early,for example in nsLayoutStatics::Initialize in the parent process.

This is a preparation for moving IndexedDatabaseManager::GetOrCreate from
FactoryOp::Open to InitializeQuotaManager.

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D189891

fix_commit_message:
Bug 1948111 - Don't re-initialize IndexedDatabaseManager::mLocale; r=dom-storage-reviewers,asuth

Differential Revision: https://phabricator.services.mozilla.com/D238593
agent_reasoning: Merged diff composed mechanically by cherry-picking fix 6dbdf1fff1e0 on top of intro 492e6f8efcbc via git's 3-way merge. Vulnerability (DataRace): The EnsureLocale() function modifies mLocale member variable from the main thread without proper synchronization, while GetLocale() reads mLocale concurrently from worker threads. This creates a data race condition: the main thread can call EnsureLocale() multiple times (through IDBFactory::AllowedForWindowInternal, WorkerPrivate::GetLoadInfo, or RemoteWorkerChild::ExecWorkerOnMainThread), potentially reallocating the string buffer while DOM worker threads are reading it via GetLocale() called in IDBFactory::OpenInternal. This can lead to use-after-free or buffer overflow when the worker thread reads memory that has been freed or reallocated by the main thread. Root cause: The EnsureLocale() function was introduced without synchronization or idempotency protection. It can be called multiple times from different code paths (IDBFactory::AllowedForWindowInternal, WorkerPrivate::GetLoadInfo, RemoteWorkerChild::ExecWorkerOnMainThread), and each call modifies the shared mLocale member. Meanwhile, DOM worker threads read this member via GetLocale() without any synchronization, creating a classic writer-reader race condition.
